_README: WHAT THIS IS: a record of what your LinkedIn profile CURRENTLY shows. Not what you
want it to show, and not what the optimizer told you to paste - what is live on the
WHY IT EXISTS: LinkedIn does two jobs in a search and both fail silently. It
generates the inbound - a profile that does not say what you now do is invisible to
the recruiters searching for exactly that, and nothing ever tells you about the leads
you did not get. And it is where your resume gets verified: a recruiter with your
resume open will pull up your profile, and any disagreement about employer, title or
dates reads as a discrepancy rather than a stale page.
So `python engine/linkedin_check.py` compares this against a resume before you send
it, and build_application.py runs the same check automatically.
WHY IT IS HAND-MAINTAINED: LinkedIn has no read API for your own profile worth
relying on, and scraping is against their terms. So this is updated by the person who
just changed the profile. That is weaker than reading the live page and far stronger
than assuming - a dated claim can at least go stale out loud.
HOW TO USE IT: open your profile, copy what each role actually says, set as_of to
today, and set confirmed true. Only employer, title and dates are compared - bullet
wording is SUPPOSED to differ between the two, so it is not checked.

experience.company: Company name exactly as your profile shows it
experience.title: Title exactly as your profile shows it
experience.dates: Month YYYY - Month YYYY, or Month YYYY - Present

_aliases_note: Deliberate naming differences between resume and profile, so they are declared once
instead of warned about on every build. Example: a resume that says 'Self-Employed'
where the profile names your LLC. Format is {"resume name": "profile name"}.
Use this ONLY for a choice you made on purpose - if the two genuinely disagree, that
is the drift this file exists to catch, and hiding it here defeats the point.
